title: Redis data structures
content: Redis is an in-memory data store supporting rich data structures: strings, hashes, lists, sets, sorted sets, streams. Session objects map naturally to hashes, allowing partial field updates without rewriting the whole session blob.

title: Memcached design
content: Memcached is a simple, multithreaded in-memory key-value cache. Values are opaque blobs up to 1MB by default. Its slab allocator and multithreaded architecture give extremely predictable latency under high concurrency.

title: Redis persistence
content: Redis offers optional persistence via RDB snapshots and AOF logs. For session caching this means sessions can survive a restart, at the cost of some write amplification. Memcached has no persistence: a restart empties the cache.

title: Replication and HA
content: Redis supports primary-replica replication, Sentinel failover, and Redis Cluster sharding out of the box. Memcached relies on client-side consistent hashing for distribution and has no built-in replication; losing a node loses its keys.

title: Session TTL semantics
content: Both Redis and Memcached support per-key TTL, which fits session expiry. Redis additionally supports touching TTLs and Lua scripts for atomic check-and-extend patterns used in sliding-window session expiry.

title: Memory efficiency
content: Memcached generally has lower per-key memory overhead for small opaque values due to its slab allocator. Redis costs more memory per key but can offload with hash-field encoding; ziplist/listpack encodings reduce small-hash overhead considerably.

title: Throughput characteristics
content: Memcached scales vertically across many threads on one node and often wins raw GET/SET throughput benchmarks. Redis is mostly single-threaded per shard for command execution (I/O threading exists since 6.0), scaling horizontally via clustering.

title: Healthcare workload constraints
content: Healthcare session data often carries PHI, so encryption in transit (TLS) and at rest, plus auditability, matter. Redis supports TLS natively and ACLs since Redis 6. Memcached supports TLS since 1.5.13 but has coarser authentication (SASL).

title: Operational tooling
content: Redis ships rich introspection: SLOWLOG, MEMORY USAGE, keyspace notifications, and a broad ecosystem (Sentinel, Cluster, RedisInsight). Memcached exposes stats counters and is famously low-maintenance due to its minimal feature surface.

title: Failure modes
content: A cold Memcached restart causes a thundering-herd of session re-creation against the backing store; mitigations include request coalescing. Redis with AOF everysec loses at most one second of session writes on crash, softening cold-start impact.

title: UNICEF India: out-of-school children and dropout
content: UNICEF India works to ensure inclusive, equitable quality education for all children. The number of out-of-school children fell from 13.46 million in 2006 to 6.1 million in 2014, yet 29% of students still drop out before completing elementary education, with the highest risk among marginalized children.

title: UNICEF India: secondary gaps and the learning crisis
content: About 50% of Indian adolescents do not complete secondary education, and an estimated 20 million children are not attending pre-school. UNICEF reports that 50% of primary school children, nearly 50 million, are not achieving grade-appropriate learning levels.

title: UNICEF India: program priorities and partners
content: UNICEF's India program prioritizes three areas: early childhood education (ECCE), out-of-school children, and quality teaching and learning. It works with the Government of India across 17 states, primarily through the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Women and Child Development.

title: NEP 2020: vision and guiding principles
content: India's National Education Policy 2020 aims to transform India into an equitable, vibrant knowledge society through high-quality education rooted in Indian ethos. Guiding principles include foundational literacy and numeracy, multidisciplinary and holistic learning, conceptual understanding over rote memorization, and multilingualism.

title: NEP 2020: the 5+3+3+4 school structure
content: NEP 2020 replaces the old 10+2 structure with a 5+3+3+4 curricular design covering ages 3 to 18: Foundational (ages 3-8), Preparatory (ages 8-11), Middle (ages 11-14), and Secondary (ages 14-18), each with a distinct pedagogical focus from play-based learning to multidisciplinary depth.

title: NEP 2020: literacy, enrolment, and language targets
content: NEP 2020 targets universal foundational literacy and numeracy for all students by Grade 3 through a National Mission, with a 2025 deadline. It also targets 100% Gross Enrolment Ratio from pre-school to Grade 12 by 2030, and mandates mother-tongue or local-language instruction until at least Grade 5.

title: NEP 2020: higher education reforms
content: NEP 2020 moves higher education toward large multidisciplinary universities, with at least one per district by 2030. It introduces a 4-year multidisciplinary undergraduate degree with multiple exit options, an Academic Bank of Credit for storing credits across institutions, and discontinues the M.Phil degree.

title: NEP 2020: research, regulation, and financing
content: NEP 2020 establishes a National Research Foundation to fund peer-reviewed research and a single higher-education regulator, HECI. It commits to increasing public investment in education to 6% of GDP at the earliest, alongside encouraging philanthropic private participation.

title: OECD Education at a Glance 2025: India's strengths
content: OECD's Education at a Glance 2025 finds India ranks in the global top five for early primary transition (44.8% of 4-year-olds already in primary school), tertiary graduates in Arts and Humanities (29.1%) and Natural Sciences and Mathematics (13.7%), and female tertiary graduates in ICT (43.7%).

title: OECD Education at a Glance 2025: India's weaknesses
content: OECD data shows India ranks near the bottom globally for upper-secondary enrolment of 15-19-year-olds (33%, rank 46 of 47) and has among the highest student-teacher ratios worldwide: 27.2 at the primary level, the highest of any country measured.

title: India: enrolment and transition trends
content: India's Gross Enrolment Ratio for Classes 1-5 improved from 114% in 2008-09 to 99% in 2013-14. Enrolment then declines sharply in higher classes: 82% in Classes 6-8, and only about 21% in higher education, compared with over 60% in the UK and Germany and 95% in the US.

title: India: drop-out rates and pupil-teacher ratios
content: The overall drop-out rate for Classes 1-8 in India is 36%, rising to 48% among Scheduled Tribes and 39% among Scheduled Castes; girls drop out less often than boys (33% versus 39%). The recommended pupil-teacher ratio of 30:1 for Classes 9-12 is exceeded in seven states, worst in Jharkhand at 68:1.

title: AISHE 2023-24: India's higher-education scale
content: The All India Survey on Higher Education 2023-24 counts 1,289 universities, 48,246 colleges, and 15,221 standalone institutions nationwide, up from 1,043 universities in 2019-20. Over 4.5 crore (45 million) students are enrolled, with a slight female majority of 49.7%.

title: AISHE 2023-24: enrolment by level and stream
content: Of India's 4.50 crore higher-education students, undergraduates are the largest group at 75.5%, followed by postgraduates at 12.9% and PhD students at 0.76%. Arts is the most popular undergraduate stream at 24.2% of enrolment, followed by Science and Commerce.

title: AISHE 2023-24: faculty and pupil-teacher ratio
content: India's higher-education system employs over 17.3 lakh (1.73 million) teachers, nearly gender-balanced. The national average pupil-teacher ratio is 25:1, but Bihar reaches 61:1 and Jharkhand 51:1, indicating significant faculty shortages in some states.

title: UNESCO 2024: arts and culture education integration
content: A UNESCO survey of 5,264 Indian educators found 73% of principals integrate arts into other subjects, but only 45.4% of arts teachers say they fully integrate culture into their teaching, with 50.8% integrating it only partially and culture often taught as facts rather than lived heritage.

title: UNESCO 2024: arts education teacher shortages
content: 60.8% of Indian school principals cite a lack of qualified arts teachers as their main recruitment challenge, and many schools rely on general classroom teachers (48.5%) or visiting artists (22.8%) instead. Over 69% of arts teachers say they urgently need professional development training.

title: UNESCO 2024: arts infrastructure gap between school types
content: Only 7.4% of Indian schools have a dedicated arts or co-curricular room. The gap is stark by school type: just 3.0% of government schools have one, versus 19.4% of private unaided schools -- a pattern UDISE+ 2021-22 data repeats across most states.
